questions.q: What does the max server memory setting control?
options: It caps the total memory the Database Engine can use — a setting every production instance should have set explicitly
It sets the size of a single database file
It only affects SQL Server Agent, not the Database Engine
It's a legacy setting with no effect on modern SQL Server
questions.explain: Left at its default (effectively unlimited), SQL Server can consume enough memory to starve the OS and other services — max server memory caps it.

questions.q: What is the buffer pool's role in SQL Server's memory architecture?
options: It's the largest memory consumer, caching data pages in memory to avoid physical disk reads
It stores compiled execution plans exclusively
It's only used during backups
It has no relationship to memory — it's a disk structure
questions.explain: The buffer pool caches data pages; it's typically the single largest consumer of SQL Server's memory footprint.

questions.q: What happens when the optimizer underestimates the memory grant needed for a sort or hash operation?
options: The operation spills to tempdb, turning a fast in-memory operation into a slower disk-bound one
SQL Server automatically increases max server memory
The query fails immediately with an error
Nothing — memory grant size has no effect on query performance
questions.explain: An underestimated memory grant (often from stale statistics or parameter sniffing) forces a spill to tempdb.

questions.q: Why is AWE (Address Windowing Extensions) not relevant to modern SQL Server memory configuration, per this lesson?
options: AWE was a legacy 32-bit memory workaround; modern SQL Server is 64-bit and doesn't need it
AWE is required on every modern SQL Server installation
AWE controls tempdb file count
AWE is a Linux-only feature
questions.explain: AWE addressed 32-bit addressing limits; it's legacy and irrelevant on 64-bit SQL Server.

questions.q: What does min server memory actually control?
options: The memory floor SQL Server won't shrink below once it has reached that level
The absolute minimum memory required just to start the service
The amount of memory reserved for SQL Server Agent
The size of the plan cache specifically
questions.explain: min server memory sets a floor: once the Engine's memory usage reaches that level, it won't release memory below it back to the OS.
